concepts.name: Definition and Classification of Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)
key_dimensions: IUCN's six-category classification system for MPAs and what distinguishes each category
Difference between 'no-take zones', 'multiple-use MPAs', and 'paper parks' — a common UPSC trap
Distinction between MPAs, Marine Reserves, and Marine Sanctuaries — overlapping terminology
CBD's Aichi Target 11 vs. post-2020 Kunming-Montreal GBF Target 3 (30x30 goal) — numerical traps

concepts.name: Legal and Institutional Framework for MPAs in India
key_dimensions: Wildlife Protection Act 1972: provisions for Marine National Parks and Marine Sanctuaries under Schedule and notification process
Environment Protection Act 1986 and Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification — overlap and jurisdictional conflicts with MPA governance
Role of MoEFCC vs. Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying — inter-ministerial conflicts
Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act 1976 — legal basis for MPA jurisdiction beyond 12 nautical miles

concepts.name: India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and MPA Governance
key_dimensions: UNCLOS provisions (Articles 55–75) vs. India's domestic legislation for EEZ-based MPA establishment
India's EEZ extent (2.02 million sq. km) vs. actual MPA coverage — the 'blue economy vs. conservation' tension
High Seas Treaty (BBNJ Agreement 2023) — relevance to Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (ABNJ) and India's position
Trap: MPAs can be declared in EEZ but enforcement and 'no-take' provisions face UNCLOS Article 56 constraints on sovereign rights

concepts.name: India's Key Marine Protected Areas: Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, and Malvan
key_dimensions: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park — first marine national park in South/Southeast Asia, biosphere reserve status, UNESCO MAB
Gulf of Kutch Marine National Park — largest marine national park in India, coral and mangrove overlap, industrial conflict (ONGC, port)
Malvan Marine Sanctuary — Maharashtra, coral reef degradation, tourism pressure
Trap: Distinguishing Marine National Park vs. Marine Sanctuary status under WPA 1972 — different restriction levels

concepts.name: Coral Reef Ecosystems within MPAs: Threats and Conservation
key_dimensions: Four major coral reef regions in India: Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar — distribution trap
Coral bleaching mechanism: thermal stress → zooxanthellae expulsion — distinction from coral death
NCSCM (National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management) vs. ZSI roles in coral monitoring
Trap: Lakshadweep corals are atoll-type (oceanic); Gulf of Mannar and Kutch are fringing reefs — type classification errors

concepts.name: Mangrove Conservation within Marine Protected Area Frameworks
key_dimensions: Mangroves under CRZ-I (A) — highest protection, no development permitted — overlap with MPA regulations
MISHTI Scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) 2023 — budget, nodal ministry
India's mangrove cover status (Sundarbans as largest; Bhitarkanika, Pichavaram) — ISFR data trap
Mangroves as 'blue carbon' sinks — carbon sequestration rate comparison with terrestrial forests (trap: mangroves sequester ~4x more carbon per unit area)

concepts.name: Seagrass Meadows as Critical MPA Habitats
key_dimensions: Seagrass as critical habitat for dugongs, sea turtles, and juvenile fish — ecological role vs. coral reefs
India's only dugong reserve: Gulf of Mannar and Andaman & Nicobar (trap: no formally notified 'Dugong Reserve' under WPA; conservation is through MPA overlap)
Seagrass blue carbon potential and its absence from most national carbon accounting frameworks
Threats: trawling, coastal runoff, climate change — policy gap in direct seagrass protection legislation in India

concepts.name: Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement and India
key_dimensions: BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty) 2023 — adopted under UNCLOS framework, key provisions: ABMT/MPAs on high seas, Marine Genetic Resources (MGR) sharing
India's negotiating position: balance between conservation and developing country rights to MGR — 'common heritage of mankind' principle
Relationship between BBNJ, CBD, and UNCLOS — jurisdictional layering (trap: BBNJ does not override UNCLOS but supplements it)
Area-Based Management Tools (ABMTs) vs. MPAs under BBNJ — distinction in legal binding nature

concepts.name: 30x30 Target (Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework) and MPA Coverage
key_dimensions: GBF Target 3: protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030 — current global MPA coverage (~8%) vs. target gap
India's current MPA coverage as % of EEZ — significantly below 30% target (trap: India's terrestrial PA coverage ~5% vs. marine <5%)
Quality vs. quantity debate: 'paper parks' problem — MPAs notified but without management plans or enforcement
Overlap with SDG 14 (Life Below Water) targets — institutional coordination trap

concepts.name: Fisheries Management and MPAs: Conflict and Co-management
key_dimensions: Traditional fishing rights vs. MPA restrictions — Constitutional angle (Article 21, right to livelihood; Article 19(1)(g))
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) vs. MPA conservation goals — blue economy tension
Community-based co-management models: Joint Forest Management equivalent for marine areas — policy gap in India
Trap: Marine Sanctuaries in India allow regulated fishing; Marine National Parks have stricter no-take provisions — a frequent confusion point

concepts.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands MPAs: Biodiversity, Strategic, and Development Conflicts
key_dimensions: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park (Wandur) — declared 1983, covers coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass
Holistic Development of Great Nicobar Island project — NITI Aayog, environment clearance controversy, proximity to MPAs and Leatherback turtle nesting sites
Andaman & Nicobar as global biodiversity hotspot overlap with Western Ghats + Indo-Burma hotspot — trap: A&N is part of Indo-Burma, not Western Ghats hotspot
Tribal protection zones (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups) overlapping with MPA governance — administrative conflict

concepts.name: Climate Change Impacts on MPAs and Ocean Acidification
key_dimensions: Ocean acidification mechanism: CO₂ → carbonic acid → reduced pH → aragonite saturation — impact on calcareous organisms
Sea level rise and MPA boundary permanence — legal/administrative challenge of shifting baselines
Marine heatwaves and MPA effectiveness: static boundaries vs. dynamic species distribution shifts
IPCC SROCC (Special Report on Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate) key findings relevant to MPA management — trap: SROCC vs. AR6 WG2 findings

concepts.name: Deep-Sea Mining and MPA Conflicts in India's Context
key_dimensions: International Seabed Authority (ISA) — regulates mining in 'the Area' (seabed beyond national jurisdiction); India holds Pioneer Investor status
India's Polymetallic nodule exploration contract with ISA — Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB) — geographic trap
Deep-sea ecosystems: hydrothermal vents, cold seeps — not typically under MPA protection in current Indian framework
Deep Ocean Mission (India, 2021) — Matsya 6000 submersible — tension between scientific exploration and conservation

concepts.name: Wetlands and Ramsar Sites: Overlap with Coastal/Marine Protection
key_dimensions: Ramsar Convention — 'wetlands of international importance' — includes coastal lagoons, estuaries, coral reefs (trap: many think Ramsar is only for freshwater wetlands)
India's Ramsar sites with marine/coastal character: Chilika, Bhitarkanika, Point Calimere, Gulf of Mannar (biosphere, not Ramsar) — classification trap
Ramsar's 3Rs (wise use principle) vs. strict MPA no-take approach — policy compatibility
Wetland Rules 2017 (amended 2022) — exclusion of certain activities — overlap with CRZ and MPA regulations

concepts.name: Marine Biodiversity Hotspots and Critically Endangered Species under MPA Protection
key_dimensions: IUCN Red List marine species in Indian waters: Dugong (Vulnerable), Whale Shark (Endangered), Olive Ridley (Vulnerable) — status trap
Project Seahorse, Turtle excluder devices (TEDs) — technology-policy interface in fisheries-MPA management
Whale Shark protection under WPA 1972 Schedule I — India first country in South Asia to protect it legally (2001)
Trap: Olive Ridley turtles nest at Gahirmatha (Odisha) — covered under Bhitarkanika NP — mass nesting called 'Arribada' — Gahirmatha is not a Marine National Park but a Marine Sanctuary

concepts.name: Blue Economy Policy Framework and MPA Integration
key_dimensions: India's Blue Economy Policy Draft (2021) — six thematic areas — absence of strong MPA integration as a critique
SAGARMALA Programme vs. MPA conservation — port-led development vs. coastal ecosystem protection
'Blue carbon' as an emerging financing mechanism — voluntary carbon markets vs. Article 6 of Paris Agreement for coastal blue carbon credits
Trap: 'Blue Economy' and 'Ocean Economy' are used interchangeably in policy but OECD distinguishes them — sustainability criterion

concepts.name: International Conventions Governing MPAs: CBD, UNCLOS, CITES, CMS
key_dimensions: CBD vs. UNCLOS jurisdictional overlap — CBD covers biodiversity within national jurisdiction; UNCLOS governs maritime zones — BBNJ bridges the gap
CITES Appendix II listings relevant to marine trade: Seahorses, Whale Sharks, Manta Rays, certain corals — trade regulation vs. MPA in-situ protection
Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) — Sharks MOU, Marine Turtles MOU — India's signatory status (trap: India signed CMS in 1983 but accession to specific MoUs varies)
IMO's Particularly Sensitive Sea Areas (PSSAs) — shipping regulation tool, different from MPAs but can overlap geographically

concepts.name: Effectiveness Metrics and Monitoring of MPAs: Science-Policy Interface
key_dimensions: Key performance indicators for MPA effectiveness: fish biomass recovery, enforcement days at sea, ecological baseline surveys — UPSC policy application angle
ProtectedSeas, MPA Atlas, and WDPA (World Database on Protected Areas) — international monitoring tools and India's data contribution gaps
MPA Management Effectiveness Tracking Tool (METT) adapted for marine context — comparison with terrestrial PA management plans under WPA
Trap: Designation of an MPA does not automatically confer protection — 'paper park' phenomenon is more prevalent in marine than terrestrial PAs globally

concepts.name: Plastic Pollution and Marine Debris: Policy Mechanisms within MPA Frameworks
key_dimensions: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Plastic Waste Management Rules 2022 — relevance to marine debris reduction
INC (Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee) for Global Plastics Treaty — India's negotiating position: focus on waste management over production caps
Ghost fishing gear — abandoned, lost, or discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) — specific threat within MPAs; FAO GPML initiative
Trap: MARPOL Annex V prohibits disposal of plastics at sea — IMO instrument, not UNCLOS — students often conflate the two

concepts.name: Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notifications and MPA Interface
key_dimensions: CRZ 2019 Notification categories: CRZ-I (ecologically sensitive including coral reefs, mangroves) — highest restrictions overlapping with MPA zones
CRZ-III A vs. CRZ-III B — population density-based classification introduced in 2019 — development permissions near MPA buffer zones
Trap: CRZ is administered by MoEFCC but through State Coastal Zone Management Authorities (SCZMAs) — different from WPA-based MPA notification process (Central + State governments)
Island-specific CRZ notifications: Island Protection Zone (IPZ) for A&N and Lakshadweep — different from mainland CRZ, stricter provisions
